sourceIssues.printed: "The Conjectures 9.1 and 9.3 cited in the statement of our main theorem asserts that this is possible" and "Theorem 1.11. Let π ⊂ A_disc(G, Q̄) with m_U(π) ≠ 0. Assume Conjectures 9.1 and 9.3; alternatively, assume π admits a parametrization as in [Laf18]."
sourceIssues.reason: (9.3) is a displayed decomposition, introduced with "for the moment we assume there is such an action, and that it gives rise to a decomposition". The numbered conjecture is Conjecture 9.5 (Lafforgue), whose part (1) asserts "There is a decomposition as in (9.3)". Noted by the extraction.

sourceIssues.printed: "We can use the standard representation of G^∨ to conclude that ν_i = 0 for all i odd. The remaining nonzero points are ν_j = ½ω^j_{⌊r_j/2⌋}, when j is odd and r_j ≥ 3, and all of these points are half-integral for G^∨."
sourceIssues.correction: "… when j is even and r_j ≥ 3 …"
sourceIssues.reason: The theorem's statement (1) lists ℜ(s) = ½h^∨ + ½Σ_{j even, r_j≥3} ε_j ω^j_{⌊r_j/2⌋}. The centralizer is Z(O^∨) = ∏_{i odd} Sp(r_i) × ∏_{j even} O(r_j), so the so(r_j) factors that carry the points are those with j even. The preceding sentence has just shown ν_i = 0 for i odd. Noted by the extraction.

sourceIssues.reason: Each item exhibits a weight i_0 where Property A fails, that is, n_u(i) = n_v(i) for i > i_0 but n_u(i_0) < n_v(i_0). The other items state exactly this with n_u on the right. As printed, "n_v(9) = 1 > 0 = n_v(9)" and "n_v(16) = 2 > 1 = n_v(16)" are self-contradictory, and "n_v(9) = n_v(9)" is vacuous. Checked on the page image. Noted by the extraction.
